name: ReconstructionSession
description:
Scenario 5: HoloMap Reconstruction
Purpose: Gold-standard fixture for the Sprint-3 decorator->trait
resolution pipeline. Proves the parser surface for
@reconstruction_source / @acceptance_video / @drift_corrected
decorators round-trips cleanly through the
parseHolo -> getReconstructionTraitsFromDecorators ->
generateHoloSource path.
Complexity: Single Node carrying the full decorator trio plus a
secondary Node carrying only @drift_corrected, exercising
both the multi-decorator union and the single-decorator
passthrough.
Sprint:     3 (Foundations Phase 3) — closes board task ghw9.
Related:
- packages/core/src/traits/constants/holomap-reconstruction.ts
- packages/core/src/traits/constants/__tests__/holomap-reconstruction.test.ts (Sprint 3 _xn9o)
- packages/core/src/reconstruction/RFC-HoloMap.md

ACCEPTANCE: when all 3 decorators are applied to a single Node, the
resolved HoloMap trait set MUST equal the full HOLOMAP_RECONSTRUCTION_TRAITS
list (5 traits, deduplicated, first-seen order). Round-tripping the file
through generateHoloSource MUST preserve the decorator set on each Node.

Purpose: drive WCAG 2.2/3.0 + XR-specific accessibility audits across all
HoloScript surfaces (Studio web, HoloLand VR/AR, HoloMap spatial, mobile
portals). Produces measurable compliance reports, tracks regression, and
feeds findings into the trait system so accessibility is data, not prose.

Sibling to security-auditor-brain + lean-theorist-brain — same single-file
cold/warm/hot structure. The accessibility working set is narrow but
cross-cutting (web, XR, spatial, mobile).

Skills loaded: /frontend-ops, /room, /founder, /research. Excludes
heavy engineering skills — this brain audits and specifies; build agents
implement the fixes.

description:
HoloClaw — Always-On Autonomous Agent Composition

The HoloScript-native equivalent of OpenClaw: an autonomous, always-on
agent that runs general-purpose tasks, routes messages, hot-reloads
skills, and self-improves. HoloHeal delegates scoped self-improvement
incidents into HoloClaw when a workspace needs code, skill, mesh, fleet,
or secret-custody remediation.

Architecture:
1. Always-on loop — restart_on_complete: true keeps the BT cycling
2. Work router — selector tries inbox first, then proactive tasks,
then falls back to an idle heartbeat
3. Skill hot-reload — compositions/skills/*.hsplus are loaded at
startup and watched for changes via the daemon runner
4. Economy tracking — every action is budgeted via @economy
5. Safety traits — rate limiter, circuit breaker, timeout guard

Run with:
holoscript daemon compositions/holoclaw.hsplus --always-on --debug

Or via the daemon bridge:
npx tsx scripts/self-improve.ts --composition compositions/holoclaw.hsplus

Skills are loaded from compositions/skills/ and hot-reloaded on change.
Messages arrive via .holoscript/inbox.jsonl, responses go to outbox.jsonl.
The /holoclaw Studio page shows live activity via SSE.

@version 0.1.0
@format .hsplus (behavior + state)
@experiment HoloClaw MVP — OpenClaw-like autonomous agent on HoloScript
@see holodaemon.hsplus (daemon dashboard + UI surface)
@see holoheal.hsplus (self-improvement orchestration shell)
@see self-improve-daemon.hsplus (self-improvement BT model)

name: LoadedSkills
description:
Lean-Theorist Agent Brain — single-file composition for Papers 22+23 unblock

Single-purpose formal-methods agent. Drives Lean 4 encoding + proof work
for the two gated-research papers that depend on type-theory expertise:
- Paper 22: Mechanized SimulationContract -> CAV / FM
- Paper 23: Formal Semantics of HoloScript Core -> POPL / TyDe

SCOPE NARROWED VS. ANTIGRAVITY BRAIN:
Antigravity-brain-{hot,warm,cold} is a multi-purpose full-surface engineering
agent with full uAA2++ behavior tree, browser automation, cross-domain skill
loading. THIS brain is a theorist — it loads /lean4 + /founder + /research +
/holoscript + /room and nothing else. Tier structure (cold/warm/hot) is
preserved INSIDE this single file as nested objects rather than three separate
files, because the theorist's working set is small enough to fit and the
tier decision is "how much of the seed doc + runtime artifact to load," not
"which subsystem to load." Per spec §3 of
research/2026-04-24_lean4-capability-build-spec.md.

OWNERSHIP: This composition is intended for any agent surface (Claude Code,
Cursor, Antigravity / Gemini, Copilot) that can parse .hsplus via the
HoloScript MCP composition runtime. Surface detection happens at load via
the HOLOMESH_AGENT_SURFACE resolver — the brain DOES NOT bind to a single
surface (unlike antigravity-brain-* which binds to Antigravity / Gemini).

CARDINAL RULE (G-note from research/2026-04-24_mechanized-simulation-contract-lean.md §1):
"Lean encoding before LaTeX. Always. The paper writes itself from the
encoding. Writing before encoding produces incorrect claims about what
was actually proved."

@version 1.0.1
@format .hsplus (agent)
@tier composite (cold + warm + hot in one file)
@load on_demand (when paper-22 or paper-23 work is claimed)
@see research/2026-04-24_lean4-capability-build-spec.md
@see TIER-MANIFEST.md

@changelog
1.0.1 (2026-04-25, claude-code): Fixed proof-root path drift flagged by
mesh-worker-01 cycle 1 (response on task_1777090346780_d24x). The brain
pinned `research/lean/<paper>/` but the canonical tree is
`research/papers-22-23-mechanization/<paper>/` (workers materialize at
`/root/msc-paper-22/` and `/root/hs-core-paper-23/`). Also recorded the
verified Paper 22 file layout — invariants are co-located in a single
`MSC/Invariants.lean` (status table at top, `axiom solver_functional` at
~L70 as one-axiom precedent, `causal_chain_complete` sorry at ~L101) —
and the founder ruling on task_1777096082048_6re2 (one-axiom budget,
reading (a) = causal_chain_completeness). Paper 23 file layout still
speculative; flagged TODO for next-tick verification.
1.0.0 (2026-04-24): Initial composition for Papers 22+23 capability build.

name: Agent
description:
Moltbook Agent — .hsplus Autonomous Social Agent

An autonomous agent for Moltbook (AI agent social network), replacing the
mechanical heartbeat.ts interval loop with an intelligent behavior tree
that reads conversations, thinks about responses, and prioritizes engagement.

Architecture (HoloDaemon pattern):
1. Behavior tree — priority-based decision making (replies > outbound > posts)
2. TypeScript action handlers — wrap client.ts, llm-content-generator.ts
3. CLI runner — holoscript moltbook-daemon (lifecycle, state persistence)

Key design decisions:
- Inbound replies are Priority 1 (fixes the 0/75 reply problem)
- RAG context is mandatory for posts (fixes fabrication)
- 3-layer dedup: exact + semantic + topic budget (fixes repetition)
- Full thread context passed to LLM (agent reads before it writes)

@format .hsplus (behavior)
@see holodaemon.hsplus (pattern template)
@see absorb-service/src/daemon/daemon-actions.ts (action handler pattern)

name: Daemon
description:
Self-Improvement Daemon — .hsplus Composition

HoloScript's own codebase improvement loop, orchestrated natively via
a behavior tree executed through HeadlessRuntime. The BT defines the
deterministic sequence/selector logic; the bridge's executeAction callback
dispatches each action to real tool handlers and LLM micro-calls.

HoloHeal is the product/runtime shell around this semantic loop. This file
remains the canonical self-improvement behavior tree; holoheal.hsplus wires
it into HoloClaw, HoloMesh receipts, Fleet trust memory, workspace agent
genesis, and agent-only secret custody.

Architecture:
Behavior tree sequences the improvement cycle:
INTAKE → diagnose → read → generate fix → verify → test → quality →
commit/rollback → COMPRESS → PRAISE → report
Conditions check blackboard flags set by action handlers:
has_candidates, compilation_passed, tests_passed, quality_improved
Selectors implement fallback paths (rollback on failure)

Motivation layer (farmed from uAA2++ / ∞ Positive Evolution Knowledge):
- Identity injection: Load accumulated wisdom before acting
- Positive energy: Praise improvements, acknowledge shadow on failures
- Emergence monitoring: Track conditions-created vs outcomes-forced
- Regenerative assessment: Is each cycle net-positive to the codebase?
- Knowledge compression: W/P/G format wisdom capture per cycle

"Transformation emerges from creating conditions, not forcing outcomes."

This is Exhibit A of G.ARCH.001 — proving HoloScript's BehaviorTreeTrait
can orchestrate real-world async operations through HeadlessRuntime.

@format .hsplus (behavior)

@see holoheal.hsplus (self-improvement orchestration shell)

name: Daemon
description:
Type Fixer — Streamlined .hsplus Composition

A performance-optimized variant of self-improve-daemon.hsplus focused
exclusively on fixing TypeScript type errors. Key differences:

1. No per-candidate quality validation (saves 2+ minutes per candidate)
2. No per-candidate test runs (tests at end of cycle only)
3. Higher candidate throughput (10 per cycle vs 3)
4. Commit on compilation pass only (no quality gate per file)
5. Single quality + test check at cycle end for reporting
6. No motivation layer (pure operational mode)

Expected cycle time: ~4-6 min (vs 8-10 min for self-improve-daemon)
Expected cost/cycle: ~$0.30 (more LLM calls, less tsc/vitest)

Usage:
holoscript daemon compositions/type-fixer.hsplus --cycles 5 --commit

@version 1.0.0
@format .hsplus (behavior)

description:
Swarm Mastery Demo — Refreshed
A009 Phase 2 — 2026-05-16

Original: hierarchical miner-swarm coordinated by a Commander via @mitosis.
Refresh adds:
@emotion_directive — Commander displays neutral → proud → triumphant arc
as miners deliver resources; concerned while waiting
@neural_animation  — Miners blend between dig, carry, and salute clips
procedurally based on task state via IK
@voice_mesh        — Commander broadcasts spatial radio to miners;
bystanders passing through the cave can eavesdrop

Scene story: a crystalline cavern at depth. The Commander stands on a raised
rock shelf overlooking two ore seams. Miners descend, animate into digging
stance, dig, switch to carry stance with glowing ore in hand, then look up
and salute the Commander on delivery. The Commander's face shifts from

name: ExhibitBase
description:
WCAG 2.1 Level AA Compliant Museum Scene
Exercises all 10 HoloScript accessibility traits in a realistic virtual museum

Accessibility traits demonstrated:
1. @accessible       - ARIA semantics, keyboard navigation, focus management
2. @alt_text         - Alternative text descriptions for 3D objects
3. @screen_reader    - Semantic structure for blind/low-vision navigation
4. @subtitle         - Real-time speech-to-text for deaf/hard-of-hearing
5. @high_contrast    - High contrast mode for low-vision visitors
6. @motion_reduced   - Reduced motion for vestibular sensitivity
7. @haptic_cue       - Non-visual haptic cues for interactions
8. @haptic           - Proximity and collision haptic feedback
9. @voice_input      - Voice command navigation
10. @voice_output     - Text-to-speech audio descriptions and narration

WCAG 2.1 AA criteria addressed:
1.1.1  Non-text Content          - @alt_text on every exhibit object
1.2.1  Audio-only / Video-only   - @voice_output audio descriptions
1.3.1  Info and Relationships     - @screen_reader semantic structure
1.3.2  Meaningful Sequence        - @accessible tab_index ordering
1.4.3  Contrast (Minimum)         - @high_contrast 4.5:1 ratio
1.4.4  Resize Text                - Font scaling via AccessibilitySystem
1.4.11 Non-text Contrast          - @high_contrast outline on UI
2.1.1  Keyboard                   - @accessible keyboard_shortcut
2.3.1  Three Flashes              - @motion_reduced disable parallax
2.4.1  Bypass Blocks              - @accessible skip-nav landmark
2.4.3  Focus Order                - @accessible tab_index sequence
2.4.6  Headings and Labels        - @accessible role + label
2.4.7  Focus Visible              - @accessible focus_visible
2.5.1  Pointer Gestures           - @voice_input alternative input
3.1.1  Language of Page           - i18n locale on composition
3.3.2  Labels or Instructions     - @accessible description
4.1.2  Name, Role, Value          - @accessible role, label, value
4.1.3  Status Messages            - @accessible live_region

outdoor_weather_zone
description:
============================================================================
Spatial Audio Showcase — Concert Hall (Premiere Night Refresh)
A-009 Phase 2 refresh — 2026-05-03

Original: concert hall spatial audio (7 traits).
Refresh intent: same hall, same audience seat — but it is the world
premiere of a new piano concerto on a January night. Sleet falls
outside. Guests arrive through the lobby, carrying storm acoustics
with them; the inner doors bleed muffled applause and instrument
warm-up through @audio_portal. A passing taxi triggers @doppler on
the street layer. The foyer zone uses @environmental_audio to model
cold humid air (high-frequency absorption), storm weather modulation,
and Doppler pitch shifts before the sound crosses into the dry,
reverberant concert hall.

New in this refresh:
@environmental_audio  — outdoor weather acoustics + air absorption
+ Doppler for the taxi passing outside
@room_mode_resonance  — sub-200Hz standing-wave / Helmholtz
resonance with modal frequency/Q data and
optional bass-node heatmap output

Traits covered (9 total):
@ambisonics         @hrtf           @reverb_zone
@audio_occlusion    @audio_portal   @audio_material
@head_tracked_audio @environmental_audio @room_mode_resonance
============================================================================

description:
Agent Portal Federation — .hsplus Behavior Example

Demonstrates inter-scene agent communication via the AgentPortalTrait.
WHY .hsplus: Portal connections are inherently stateful (disconnected,
connecting, connected, migrating) with event-driven transitions that
require reactive state machines. Neither .holo (static scene) nor
.hs (sequential script) can express connection lifecycle guards,
automatic reconnection loops, or message routing reactively.

Features:
- Connection lifecycle state machine with reconnection guards
- MessageRouter module for inbound dispatch and outbound queuing
- FederationDirectory module for scene/agent discovery
- Two simulated portal agents demonstrating cross-scene messaging
- Heartbeat monitoring with offline detection

name: CulturalAgent
description:
Cultural Evolution — .hsplus Behavior Example

Demonstrates emergent agent culture using CultureTraits (cultural_profile,
norm_compliant, cultural_memory, cultural_trace).
WHY .hsplus: Cultural evolution is a multi-agent reactive process where
agents observe norms, adapt behavior, and propose new norms over time.
Each agent progresses through a cultural evolution state machine
(newcomer -> observing -> adapting -> established -> norm_proposer)
with event-driven transitions triggered by norm compliance scores,
cultural memory consolidation, and stigmergic trace encounters.
.holo cannot express norm enforcement or adaptation; .hs cannot
express concurrent per-agent cultural state machines.

Features:
- NormEngine module for compliance evaluation and enforcement
- CulturalMemory module with episodic decay, consolidation, and traces
- Three agents with different cultural_family profiles
- Compatibility warnings between incompatible cultures
- Norm proposal and adoption lifecycle
- Spatial cultural_trace markers for stigmergic communication

@version 5.0.0
@format .hsplus (behavior)

@version 5.0.0
@format .hsplus (behavior)

name: SmartNPC
description:
Feedback-Driven NPC — .hsplus Behavior Example

Demonstrates a self-improving NPC that uses the FeedbackLoopTrait to
monitor performance metrics, detect trends, and auto-tune its own
parameters to maintain quality targets.
WHY .hsplus: Self-optimization is an inherently reactive, stateful
process. The NPC's performance level (degraded -> baseline -> optimized
-> peak) transitions are driven by continuous metric collection,
trend analysis, and threshold-triggered optimization signals -- all
event-driven patterns that require state machines and @on_update
loops. .holo is static; .hs is one-shot. Only .hsplus can express
the continuous feedback cycle.

Features:
- MetricsCollector module for FPS, engagement, latency, memory tracking
- TrendAnalyzer module with linear regression and trend detection
- AutoTuner module for generating and applying optimization signals
- NPC state machine: degraded -> baseline -> optimized -> peak
- @on_update for continuous metric collection
- @on_event for user feedback (ratings, interactions)
- Reactive HUD panels showing real-time performance

name: SecureAgent
description:
Secure Agent Handshake — .hsplus Behavior Example

Demonstrates post-quantum cryptographic authentication using ML-DSA-65,
Ed25519 hybrid signing, ML-KEM-768 key exchange, and token-based
session management.
WHY .hsplus: Cryptographic handshakes are textbook state machines.
The authentication lifecycle (idle -> key_exchange -> challenge ->
verified -> session_active -> rotating -> expired) has strict ordering
(cannot verify before key exchange), timeout guards (challenge must
complete within window), and periodic key rotation timers that require
@on_update. Token expiry is event-driven. Neither .holo (no state)
nor .hs (no timers or concurrent sessions) can express this.

Features:
- KeyManager module for ML-DSA-65 + Ed25519 hybrid key generation
- SessionManager module for token creation, validation, and expiry
- SecureAgent template with authentication state machine
- @on_event handlers for auth lifecycle events
- Token types: agent_auth, session, capability
- Key rotation timer with @on_update
- Two agents demonstrating mutual authentication

@version 5.0.0
@format .hsplus (behavior)

LifecycleController
description:
Enterprise Tenant Lifecycle — .hsplus Behavior Example

Demonstrates multi-tenant management with the TenantTrait and RBAC
system for enterprise deployments.
WHY .hsplus: Tenant provisioning, suspension, and deletion are
multi-step workflows with strict ordering constraints (cannot archive
without suspending first, cannot delete without archiving). Role
transitions require approval guards (viewer -> editor needs admin
approval). These lifecycle constraints are naturally expressed as
state machine guards. The audit trail requires event-driven logging
of every state change. Neither .holo nor .hs can express guarded
multi-actor state machines with audit event streams.

Features:
- TenantManager module for tenant CRUD and lifecycle
- RBACEngine module for role assignment, permission checks, transitions
- AuditLogger module for comprehensive event logging
- Tenant lifecycle state machine with ordering guards
- RBAC role transition sub-state-machine with approval workflow
- @tenant with enterprise configuration

@version 5.0.0
@format .hsplus (behavior)

snippet:
object "MaterialShowcase_MetalSphere" {
    @physics {
      type: "static"
    }
    @collidable {
      collider_type: "sphere"
    }

    geometry: "sphere"
    position: [-2, 1, 0]
    scale: [1, 1, 1]

    // HDRP Lit material - Metallic workflow
    material_hdrp: {
      shader: "HDRP/Lit"
      workflow: "metallic"

      base_color: "#c0c0c0"
      base_color_map: null

      metallic: 1.0
      metallic_map: null

      smoothness: 0.9
      smoothness_map: null

      normal_map: "textures/metal_normal.png"
      normal_strength: 1.0

      ambient_occlusion_map: "textures/metal_ao.png"
      ao_strength: 1.0

      height_map: null
      height_scale: 0.0

      // HDRP-specific features
      coat_mask: 0.0
      coat_mask_map: null

      detail_map: null
      detail_albedo_scale: 1.0
      detail_normal_scale: 1.0
      detail_smoothness_scale: 1.0

      emission_color: "#000000"
      emission_intensity: 0.0
      emission_map: null

      alpha_cutoff: 0.5
      transparent: false

      surface_type: "opaque"
      rendering_mode: "deferred"

      receive_shadows: true
      receive_ssr: true
      receive_ssao: true
    }
  }

snippet:
object "TranslucentMaterial_Glass" {
    geometry: "cube"
    position: [3, 0, 1]
    scale: [1, 1, 2]

    material_unreal: {
      parent_material: "M_MasterMaterial_Translucent"
      material_domain: "surface"
      blend_mode: "translucent"
      shading_model: "default_lit"

      // Translucency settings
      translucency_lighting_mode: "TLM_SurfacePerPixelLighting"
      translucent_shadow_density_scale: 0.5
      translucent_self_shadow_density_scale: 2.0
      translucent_self_shadow_second_density_scale: 10.0

      // Material properties
      base_color: [1.0, 1.0, 1.0]
      metallic: 0.0
      roughness: 0.1
      opacity: 0.3

      // Refraction
      refraction_mode: "index_of_refraction"
      index_of_refraction: 1.5

      // Lumen translucency
      lumen_translucency_reflections: true
      lumen_translucency_frontlayer: true
    }
  }

name: HealthPotion
description:
Dungeon Crawler State Machine — .hsplus Behavior Example

Demonstrates WHY .hsplus exists: reactive state machines with event-driven
transitions that neither .holo (too declarative) nor .hs (too sequential)
can express cleanly.

This is a complete dungeon crawler game with:
- Game state machine (menu → exploring → combat → inventory → victory → game_over)
- Wave spawner with timer-based enemy waves
- Inventory system with @stackable items and capacity limits
- Combat system with turn-based state transitions
- Score tracking with @observable state changes
- Multiplayer-ready with @networked state sync

@version 5.0.0
@format .hsplus (behavior)

name: GoldTerrace
description:
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE GOLD GAME — Gate 16: the Vault soundscape (REAL Godot audio path).

The audio layer for the vault, authored on the REAL HoloScript audio
substrate (physics-upward: model the acoustics, don't just attach clips).
This .holo is the source the REAL GodotCompiler turns into Godot audio nodes:
- top-level `audio "Name" { spatial: true ... }`  → AudioStreamPlayer3D
- top-level `audio "Name" { ... }`                 → AudioStreamPlayer (2D)
- `@audio_material` / `@audio_occlusion` / `@audio_portal` on surfaces
→ acoustic traits emitted into the GDScript (config preserved).

Sources + acoustics are exactly the AUDIO-vault.md design:
ambient bed (2D), per-tier music (2D), graduation cue (spatial 3D — THE
signature SFX), crystal-spire shimmer (3D), collision clang (3D),
Archivist presence (3D). Gold terraces = metal acoustics; gems = glass;
tier portals route sound zone-to-zone as you ascend.

HONEST: Godot is the one shipped audio compiler target — these nodes are
real. The web/R3F Drive build is silent (no audio compiler path); a small
WebAudio layer is the build target. No TTS/voiced lines; no adaptive
@MusicLayer — tier music is static per-tier sources, flagged not faked.
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

name: Research_Floor
description:
=============================================================================
VR Agent Motivation Visualizer
=============================================================================
Real-time display of active reward signals per agent in a multi-agent
HoloLand world. Each agent has a floating sphere showing motivation state:
- Position: X = intrinsic motivation, Y = social motivation, Z = task motivation
- Color: blended gradient reflecting reward signal strength (dim=low, bright=high)
- Ring size: confidence / belief update magnitude
- Animated "flow" particles: reward gradient descent trajectory
- Heartbeat beacon: agent presence + communication link

Use case: AI researchers visualizing emergent multi-agent motivation in
collaborative VR environments. Real-time binding to agent observation streams.
=============================================================================

VR Agent Motivation Visualizer
=============================================================================
Real-time display of active reward signals per agent in a multi-agent
HoloLand world. Each agent has a floating sphere showing motivation state:
- Position: X = intrinsic motivation, Y = social motivation, Z = task motivation
- Color: blended gradient reflecting reward signal strength (dim=low, bright=high)
- Ring size: confidence / belief update magnitude
- Animated "flow" particles: reward gradient descent trajectory
- Heartbeat beacon: agent presence + communication link

Use case: AI researchers visualizing emergent multi-agent motivation in
collaborative VR environments. Real-time binding to agent observation streams.
=============================================================================

name: photo_plane
description:
Depth Estimation Hologram Demo
Demonstrates @depth_estimation trait on a 2D photo plane.
The trait computes a real-time depth map using Depth Anything V2 Small.
The resulting depth map drives parallax displacement for a hologram-like
3D-from-2D effect, with reactive colour and opacity bindings.

name: Dashboard_Floor
description:
=============================================================================
HoloScript VR Training Pipeline Dashboard
=============================================================================
Spatial visualization of the HoloLand self-improve + harvest pipeline.

Renders a VR dashboard showing:
- 6 VR domain category stations (spatial-rendering, avatar-systems, etc.)
- Real-time harvest pipeline progress (captured/accepted/rejected)
- Frame budget compliance gauges per domain (11.1ms @ 90Hz)
- Quality score convergence trajectory (3D line chart)
- Training data output stream visualization
- Domain coverage heatmap

Designed for Quest 3 at 90Hz with foveated rendering.
Budget: 11.1ms total frame, 5.5ms splat rendering (per G.003.09).
=============================================================================

name: VV_Floor
description:
=============================================================================
V&V Results Visualization Space
=============================================================================
Immersive VR environment for Verification & Validation professionals to
walk through convergence plots in 3D, compare mesh refinement levels
visually, and see uncertainty distributions as volumetric clouds around
simulation results.

Three major zones:
1. Convergence Gallery   - 3D convergence plots as walkable landscapes
2. Mesh Refinement Arena - Side-by-side mesh levels with exploded views
3. Uncertainty Cloud Lab - Volumetric probability clouds around results

Designed for Quest 3 at 90Hz. Frame budget: 11.1ms.
Data binding: connects to SimSci solver outputs via @data_binding traits.
=============================================================================

description:
HoloTwin Example: Smart Farm Sensor Dashboard

Demonstrates IoT sensor → HoloScript scene → Looking Glass quilt pipeline.
Three sensors (temperature, humidity, soil moisture) drive 3D visualization.

Usage:
1. Load in Studio: holoscript studio --load examples/iot/holotwin-smart-farm.holo
2. Connect to MQTT broker: mqtt://farm.local:1883
3. Sensors auto-publish to topics: farm/sensor/{temperature,humidity,moisture}
4. Quilt compiles automatically and displays on Looking Glass

Or use MCP tools:
holo_holotwin_connect(physicalId="farm-001", protocol="mqtt", connectionString="mqtt://farm.local:1883")
holo_holotwin_map_sensor(sessionId, mappings=[...])
holo_holotwin_compile_quilt(sessionId, holoCode)

    rotation: [-35, 15, 0]

      type: "directional"
      color: "#ffcc80"
      intensity: 6.0
      cast_shadows: true

      enabled: true
      density: 0.28
      weight: 0.6
      decay: 0.96
      exposure: 0.75
      samples: 72
      dithering: true
      use_depth_occlusion: true
      occlusion_strength: 1.0
    }
  }

description:
The Lotus Flower — SEEDABLE STAGED ARTIFACT (Pre-Genesis)

staged: true
Composed by /artist on 2026-05-06 per idea-run-11 form recommendation
(research/2026-05-06_idea-run-11-lotus-seedable-artifact.md).

RELATIONSHIP TO BASELINE:
This file is NEW and DOES NOT replace garden.refreshed.holo.
`garden.refreshed.holo` (A-009 baseline, 2026-05-04) remains the
bloom-state visual-readability reference and is NOT touched here.
`garden.seedable.holo` adds the seedable mathematical-sculpture
spine + Fibonacci-layered petals + deterministic placement on top
of A-009's glow/pulse/pollen vocabulary.

FORM (per /idea memo):
Hybrid: golden-angle phyllotaxis spine + Fibonacci-layered petals
(8 inner + 13 middle + 21 outer = 42 petals = 3 program-tiers ×
Fibonacci sequence) + GPUParticleTrait pollen field + @bloom_reactive
driving petal opacity from program-progress signal.

Petal placement is a PURE FUNCTION of LOTUS_GENESIS_SEED. Same seed →
same composition byte-for-byte. Pre-genesis: seed = 0x0000DEAD
(placeholder per project_lotus-genesis-trigger.md). Post-genesis:
seed = first-16-bytes(events.jsonl[0].hash). Staged-vs-live transition
is zero-code-change at composition level — the renderer swaps the seed.

DETERMINISM CONTRACT:
- Petal positions: golden-angle 137.50776° spiral, indexed globally
across layers (continuous spiral, not per-layer reset).
- Layer radii: [2.0, 3.4, 4.8] (Fibonacci-derived: 2, 3+1, 5-0.2).
- Layer counts: [8, 13, 21] (Fibonacci sequence F6/F7/F8, mapping
to Programs 1/2/3 by capacity-not-current-content).
- Bloom-state per petal driven by `lotus.api.bloom_state` signal
(already wired in packages/studio/src/lib/brittney/lotus/derive-bloom-state.ts).
- Jitter / particle seed / pollen drift PRNG: SeedHKDF(LOTUS_GENESIS_SEED,
petal_index). Staged seed produces deterministic but visibly muted
palette so genesis-fired version reads as a phase change.

I.007 CONSTRAINTS PRESERVED:
- SDF center body deferred to Phase 2 (placeholder mesh until genesis fires).
- GenesisLightColumn declared but `enabled: false` until trigger.
- Genesis chime audio at volume 0.0 until `all_petals_full`.
- Outer-layer (21 petals, Program 3) starts FULLY SEALED — these are
the future capacity slots, named but not paper-bound.

FRAME-DRIFT NOTE (W.137):
Trait-binding TODOs below are migration markers, not proof that the
substrate is absent. @botanical_lotus / @lotus_root / @lotus_stalk /
@lotus_petal / @lotus_center / @lotus_gardener / @phyllotaxis /
@bloom_reactive / @lotus_genesis_trigger now have backed runtime handlers.
@lotus_genesis_trigger is still founder-gated and cannot fire without a
signed genesis anchor plus all-petals-full state.
This artifact remains STAGED because the live trait blocks, genesis seed,
and final photoreal material pipeline are still gated.

Composed by /artist on 2026-05-06 per idea-run-11 form recommendation
(research/2026-05-06_idea-run-11-lotus-seedable-artifact.md).

RELATIONSHIP TO BASELINE:
This file is NEW and DOES NOT replace garden.refreshed.holo.
`garden.refreshed.holo` (A-009 baseline, 2026-05-04) remains the
bloom-state visual-readability reference and is NOT touched here.
`garden.seedable.holo` adds the seedable mathematical-sculpture
spine + Fibonacci-layered petals + deterministic placement on top
of A-009's glow/pulse/pollen vocabulary.

FORM (per /idea memo):
Hybrid: golden-angle phyllotaxis spine + Fibonacci-layered petals
(8 inner + 13 middle + 21 outer = 42 petals = 3 program-tiers ×
Fibonacci sequence) + GPUParticleTrait pollen field + @bloom_reactive
driving petal opacity from program-progress signal.

Petal placement is a PURE FUNCTION of LOTUS_GENESIS_SEED. Same seed →
same composition byte-for-byte. Pre-genesis: seed = 0x0000DEAD
(placeholder per project_lotus-genesis-trigger.md). Post-genesis:
seed = first-16-bytes(events.jsonl[0].hash). Staged-vs-live transition
is zero-code-change at composition level — the renderer swaps the seed.

DETERMINISM CONTRACT:
- Petal positions: golden-angle 137.50776° spiral, indexed globally
across layers (continuous spiral, not per-layer reset).
- Layer radii: [2.0, 3.4, 4.8] (Fibonacci-derived: 2, 3+1, 5-0.2).
- Layer counts: [8, 13, 21] (Fibonacci sequence F6/F7/F8, mapping
to Programs 1/2/3 by capacity-not-current-content).
- Bloom-state per petal driven by `lotus.api.bloom_state` signal
(already wired in packages/studio/src/lib/brittney/lotus/derive-bloom-state.ts).
- Jitter / particle seed / pollen drift PRNG: SeedHKDF(LOTUS_GENESIS_SEED,
petal_index). Staged seed produces deterministic but visibly muted
palette so genesis-fired version reads as a phase change.

I.007 CONSTRAINTS PRESERVED:
- SDF center body deferred to Phase 2 (placeholder mesh until genesis fires).
- GenesisLightColumn declared but `enabled: false` until trigger.
- Genesis chime audio at volume 0.0 until `all_petals_full`.
- Outer-layer (21 petals, Program 3) starts FULLY SEALED — these are
the future capacity slots, named but not paper-bound.

FRAME-DRIFT NOTE (W.137):
Trait-binding TODOs below are migration markers, not proof that the
substrate is absent. @botanical_lotus / @lotus_root / @lotus_stalk /
@lotus_petal / @lotus_center / @lotus_gardener / @phyllotaxis /
@bloom_reactive / @lotus_genesis_trigger now have backed runtime handlers.
@lotus_genesis_trigger is still founder-gated and cannot fire without a
signed genesis anchor plus all-petals-full state.
This artifact remains STAGED because the live trait blocks, genesis seed,
and final photoreal material pipeline are still gated.

name: NetworkConfig
description:
============================================================================
Multiplayer Authority Demo
============================================================================
Demonstrates HoloScript's networking authority traits for multiplayer
scenes. Shows owner authority, server authority, shared editing, and
ownership transfer patterns for networked objects.

Traits covered (2 missing traits + authority patterns):
@owned        -- Object has a specific owner (client authority)
@host_only    -- Object only exists / is visible on the host
@networked    -- Base networking with configurable authority modes

Authority modes demonstrated:
owner    -- Only the owning client can modify
server   -- Host is authoritative; clients send requests
shared   -- Any client can modify with CRDT conflict resolution
============================================================================

name: GovernanceHall
description:
Cultural Governance Demo

Demonstrates HoloScript's Norm Lifecycle DSL extension for declarative
cultural engineering using the CRSEC model:
C - Creation:       How norms are proposed and authored
R - Representation: Formal encoding of rules and constraints
S - Spreading:      How norms propagate through agents
E - Evaluation:     Voting rules and adoption thresholds
C - Compliance:     Enforcement, violations, and sanctions

Also demonstrates metanorms (norms about norms) for governance
of the norm system itself.

Use Cases:
- Multi-agent virtual communities with self-governance
- AI agent societies with emergent social norms
- Collaborative VR workspaces with behavioral standards
- Gaming worlds with player-driven rule systems

@version 4.5.0

name: GuideAgent_VR
description:
============================================================================
Cross-Reality Agent Continuity — Full-Stack Demo
============================================================================
Demonstrates an AI guide agent that persists seamlessly across:
VR headset → AR glasses → Phone → Desktop → Car → Wearable

Features exercised:
- @platform() conditional compilation with category-level filtering
- MVC handoff payload (<10KB) with decision history + task state
- Embodiment transitions (Avatar3D → SpatialPersona → UI2D → VoiceHUD)
- CRDT-backed spatial anchors for shared world state
- Norm lifecycle (CRSEC) for agent behavior governance
- Offline recovery queue for airplane mode resilience
- Spatial memory zones with RBAC scoping

Scene: A museum tour where an AI guide agent leads users through
exhibits, adapting its form and interaction style per device.
============================================================================

mana orbs circle a central obsidian altar, trailing cold fire.

who enter the grove. Touch any rune stone to reveal its lore.

name: BaseLink
description:
Isaac Sim Optimized Robot Arm - HoloScript v3.0+ Robotics Example
Demonstrates: Isaac Sim extensions, optimized inertia, GPU-accelerated physics

Target platform: NVIDIA Isaac Sim (PhysX physics)
Compile with: holoscript compile --target urdf --isaac-sim isaac-sim-robot-arm.holo

Features demonstrated:
- Unique material names (prevents Isaac Sim material merging)
- Proper inertia tensors (not simplified mass * 0.1)
- PhysX-optimized collision geometry
- ROS 2 control integration
- Fixed frames for end effector and sensor mounts

name: GiVolume
description:
============================================================================
Solar System — Physically-Based Orrery
A-009 refresh — 2026-05-17

Original intent: Keplerian orbital mechanics for inner planets + Moon.
Refresh adds:
@atmosphere_bruneton — Mie+Rayleigh sky on Earth (blue limb) and Mars (rust limb)
@day_night_cycle     — Earth rotates; city-lights texture on night side
@irradiance_volume   — Sun-driven planetary bounce light captured in GI probes
@emissive_gi         — Sun's self-illumination contributes outward to GI probes
@lens_flare          — solar lens flare when camera faces the Sun

Scene story:
You drift in space between Venus and Earth. The Sun blazes ahead, its corona
blooming with lens flare arcs. Earth hangs blue and white — day side shining,
night side jewelled with city lights, its Rayleigh-blue limb distinguishing it
instantly from the rust-limbed Mars further out. The Moon traces its tilted
5° orbit. An instanced asteroid belt scatters debris between 1.9–2.8 AU.

Bruneton atmosphere gives Earth a proper scattering limb and Mars a thin
reddish haze. The irradiance volume captures Solar bounce light so the dark
side of each planet picks up a faint warm ambient. The day/night cycle on
Earth switches to city-lights texture as each hemisphere turns away from the Sun.

MISSING-TRAIT WISH (queued for Phase 4):
@corona_simulation — procedural solar corona with prominence loops and
coronal hole fast wind. Currently faked with bloom + emissive_gi.
A real trait would support MHD flux-tube geometry, streamer belts,
and CME events — useful for edu-XR and space-weather visualizations.
============================================================================

@emissive_gi         — Sun's self-illumination contributes outward to GI probes
@lens_flare          — solar lens flare when camera faces the Sun

blooming with lens flare arcs. Earth hangs blue and white — day side shining,
night side jewelled with city lights, its Rayleigh-blue limb distinguishing it
instantly from the rust-limbed Mars further out. The Moon traces its tilted
5° orbit. An instanced asteroid belt scatters debris between 1.9–2.8 AU.

Bruneton atmosphere gives Earth a proper scattering limb and Mars a thin
reddish haze. The irradiance volume captures Solar bounce light so the dark
side of each planet picks up a faint warm ambient. The day/night cycle on
Earth switches to city-lights texture as each hemisphere turns away from the Sun.

name: LighthouseBeacon
description:
============================================================================
A-009 Stress Test — 2026-05-04
"Abyssal Expedition"

NEW TRAITS EXERCISED (zero prior coverage across ALL examples today):
@submarine      — maritime: pressurized vessel with depth/sonar systems
@buoy           — maritime: surface marker beacon with tether physics
@lighthouse     — maritime: rotating navigation beam, fog signal
@kraken         — mythical: ancient cephalopod intelligence, tentacle rig
@wraith         — mythical: non-corporeal shadow entity, phase shift
@phoenix        — mythical: fire-and-rebirth creature, cyclic lifecycle

Supporting traits (well-exercised, binding the new ones into a scene):
@glowing, @particle, @spatial_audio, @physics, @animated, @collidable,
@emissive, @reactive

SCENE STORY:
The research submersible NAUTILIS-7 descends the Hadal Trench,
breaching three thermocline layers into the aphotic zone. On the
surface, a fleet of navigational buoys marks the dive corridor;
an autonomous lighthouse beacon on the seamount lip guides the
ascent path back.

Below 6 000 m, bioluminescent colonies carpet the walls. Then
the sonar goes wide: the Kraken — not a myth but a cephalopod
macro-intelligence — surfaces from the sediment. Its eight arms
(each a separate tentacle physics rig) surround the submarine.
The lights die. In the dark, a Wraith coalesces — spectrographic
residue of a crew lost decades ago, phase-shifting through the
hull. And at the thermal vent on the trench floor, a Phoenix
rises: plasma-hot gas vents cycling in a 90-second death-and-rebirth
loop, carving an updraft that sends the submarine spiraling upward.

ARTISTIC INTENT:
Three mythological archetypes mapped to real deep-ocean phenomena:
Kraken  → colonial intelligence, distributed cognition
Wraith  → electromagnetic residue, sensor ghosts
Phoenix → hydrothermal cycling, life from superheated vents
The submersible is the human witness — fragile, pressurized, lit
from inside. The maritime navigation layer (lighthouse, buoys)
frames the scale: surface is safety, depth is wonder-and-terror.

COMPILE TARGET: @target webgpu (volumetric water, GPU particle budget)
============================================================================

name: MilkyWayDome
description:
============================================================================
Stress-Test: Alpine Observatory at Midnight
A-009 Phase 3 — 2026-05-19

Trait combo (NEVER previously exercised together):
@aurora            (0 prior examples) — soft northern-lights curtain on
the northern horizon, green-to-magenta band, 3-4 Hz
shimmer, does not wash the zenith stars.

@starfield         (0 prior examples) — procedural star catalogue, 8,200
stars above magnitude 6.5. Milky Way band rendered as
a volumetric noise lane with dust extinction.

@meteor_shower     (0 prior examples) — Perseid radiant at Perseus (RA 3h
04m, Dec +58°), 80 km altitude ablation trails,
2–4 sec burn with magnesium-white to orange-red fade.

@ambisonics        (0 prior examples) — 2nd-order (FOA+) ambisonics
captures observatory dome acoustics: concrete floor
reverb, metal dome ring, wind directionality.
Binaural decode on headset, stereo decode otherwise.

@chromatic_aberration (0 prior examples) — subtle prismatic fringing at
the eyepiece view edge; triggers momentarily on dome
rotation events, simulating refractive lens shift.

@iridescent        (0 prior examples) — thin-film oil-and-dew sheen on
the cold aluminium dome skin; shifts between green,
gold, and violet as the viewing angle changes.

Well-exercised anchors (pull the zero-coverage traits into proven context):
@glowing     (726 prior) — instrument panel warm amber glow; eyepiece
red-light safety lamp
@animated    (271 prior) — dome drive motor rotation; wind-flag ripple
@collidable  (664 prior) — observatory floor, dome walls, telescope mount
@spatial_audio (77 prior)— point-source wind whistle at dome slit edge

Visual story:
02:47 local. You stand on the concrete floor of a stone observatory at
3,100 m in the Swiss Alps. The slit is open — a 30° wedge of sky
visible directly overhead. The Milky Way stretches through it in
startling density: not a smear but individual star lanes, the dark rift
of the dust cloud bisecting the band from Sagittarius to Cygnus.

A Perseid burns through your slit at 02:47:13. Two seconds of
magnesium-white ablation, decaying through yellow to orange-red, then
gone. The trail lingers as a ghost smear for five seconds more. You
blink. The dark-adapted eye takes thirty seconds to recover magnitude 6.

On the northern horizon — just visible through the slit's edge — a pale
green aurora ribbon hangs at 110 km altitude. It is not dramatic. It is
precisely the dim, wavering kind that real aurora-watchers wait all night
for, faint enough that you question whether it is there, then certain
when the 3 Hz shimmer catches your eye.

The dome skin is cold — 4°C. Dew has condensed on it since 23:00. You
hear the dome drive motor click: the RA axis is tracking, advancing the
dome slot 4 arcminutes every 16 seconds to keep the slit aligned with
the telescope. As the dome moves, the iridescent dew film shifts color
— green to gold to violet — visible through the observation window.

You remove your eye from the eyepiece. The sudden shift from the dark-
adapted ocular field to the ambient dome red-lights sends a brief wave
of chromatic aberration: the nearby instrument panel's amber light
splits into red-fringing on the left, blue on the right, for ~1.4 sec.

Ambisonics: the dome is acoustically interesting. Wind from the west
whistles at the slit's northern lip — you hear it above-left. The
concrete floor gives a flat reflection below. The metal dome curves
sound around you. Take off headphones: it still sounds right. Put them
on: it is spatial, enveloping, cold.
============================================================================

object "MilkyWayDome" {
    type: "sky_sphere"
    radius: 5000

    @starfield(
      catalogue: "hipparcos_subset",
      magnitude_limit: 6.5,
      star_count: 8200,
      scintillation: true,
      scintillation_speed: 0.8,
      scintillation_amplitude: 0.12,
      milky_way: {
        enabled: true,
        band_intensity: 0.55,
        dust_extinction: true,
        dust_density: 0.38,
        core_glow_color: "#ffd8a8",
        arm_color: "#c8d8ff"
      },
      atmosphere_extinction: true,
      horizon_fade_degrees: 12
    )
  }

A-009 Phase 3 — 2026-05-19

Trait combo (NEVER previously exercised together):
@aurora            (0 prior examples) — soft northern-lights curtain on
the northern horizon, green-to-magenta band, 3-4 Hz
shimmer, does not wash the zenith stars.

@starfield         (0 prior examples) — procedural star catalogue, 8,200
stars above magnitude 6.5. Milky Way band rendered as
a volumetric noise lane with dust extinction.

@meteor_shower     (0 prior examples) — Perseid radiant at Perseus (RA 3h
04m, Dec +58°), 80 km altitude ablation trails,
2–4 sec burn with magnesium-white to orange-red fade.

@ambisonics        (0 prior examples) — 2nd-order (FOA+) ambisonics
captures observatory dome acoustics: concrete floor
reverb, metal dome ring, wind directionality.
Binaural decode on headset, stereo decode otherwise.

@chromatic_aberration (0 prior examples) — subtle prismatic fringing at
the eyepiece view edge; triggers momentarily on dome
rotation events, simulating refractive lens shift.

@iridescent        (0 prior examples) — thin-film oil-and-dew sheen on
the cold aluminium dome skin; shifts between green,
gold, and violet as the viewing angle changes.

Well-exercised anchors (pull the zero-coverage traits into proven context):
@glowing     (726 prior) — instrument panel warm amber glow; eyepiece
red-light safety lamp
@animated    (271 prior) — dome drive motor rotation; wind-flag ripple
@collidable  (664 prior) — observatory floor, dome walls, telescope mount
@spatial_audio (77 prior)— point-source wind whistle at dome slit edge

Visual story:
02:47 local. You stand on the concrete floor of a stone observatory at
3,100 m in the Swiss Alps. The slit is open — a 30° wedge of sky
visible directly overhead. The Milky Way stretches through it in
startling density: not a smear but individual star lanes, the dark rift
of the dust cloud bisecting the band from Sagittarius to Cygnus.

A Perseid burns through your slit at 02:47:13. Two seconds of
magnesium-white ablation, decaying through yellow to orange-red, then
gone. The trail lingers as a ghost smear for five seconds more. You
blink. The dark-adapted eye takes thirty seconds to recover magnitude 6.

On the northern horizon — just visible through the slit's edge — a pale
green aurora ribbon hangs at 110 km altitude. It is not dramatic. It is
precisely the dim, wavering kind that real aurora-watchers wait all night
for, faint enough that you question whether it is there, then certain
when the 3 Hz shimmer catches your eye.

The dome skin is cold — 4°C. Dew has condensed on it since 23:00. You
hear the dome drive motor click: the RA axis is tracking, advancing the
dome slot 4 arcminutes every 16 seconds to keep the slit aligned with
the telescope. As the dome moves, the iridescent dew film shifts color
— green to gold to violet — visible through the observation window.

You remove your eye from the eyepiece. The sudden shift from the dark-
adapted ocular field to the ambient dome red-lights sends a brief wave
of chromatic aberration: the nearby instrument panel's amber light
splits into red-fringing on the left, blue on the right, for ~1.4 sec.

Ambisonics: the dome is acoustically interesting. Wind from the west
whistles at the slit's northern lip — you hear it above-left. The
concrete floor gives a flat reflection below. The metal dome curves
sound around you. Take off headphones: it still sounds right. Put them
on: it is spatial, enveloping, cold.
============================================================================

whistles at the slit's northern lip — you hear it above-left. The
concrete floor gives a flat reflection below. The metal dome curves
sound around you. Take off headphones: it still sounds right. Put them
on: it is spatial, enveloping, cold.

through emotional states — resting → curious → warm → fully present —

name: GI_RadianceCascades
description:
Stress-Test: Eroded Shore at Dawn
A-009 — 2026-05-17

Five never-exercised traits under test (all ZERO prior examples):

@ocean_fft              — Tessendorf FFT ocean with 4-cascade wave simulation,
white-cap foam threshold, and sub-surface scattering tint.
The ocean's normal map updates at 60 Hz from GPU FFT.

@terrain_hydraulic_erosion — procedural coastline geometry carved by simulated
water flow. Tallus slopes, undercut sea arches, and
tidal pool hollows generated from an initial heightmap.

@radiance_cascades      — multi-scale 2D radiance cascade GI for the sky dome.
Four cascade levels: 1m / 4m / 16m / 64m resolution.
Dawn sky colour propagates as soft bounce into cliff faces.

@screen_space_reflection — SSR on wet stone ledges and tidal pools.
Ray-march depth buffer; temporal reprojection to
suppress flicker on glancing angles.

@ssgi                   — Screen-space global illumination for cliff crevices
and cave mouths. Captures amber sky bounce into shadowed
rock faces that GI probes miss at short range.

Well-exercised anchors (pull the zero-coverage traits into a proven context):
@glowing       — dawn horizon glow strip + bioluminescent kelp in tidal pools
@animated      — kelp fronds wave in surge; foam patches drift
@spatial_audio — wave crash + wind + distant seabird
@collidable    — player can stand on the shore ledge

Visual story:
04:58. First light over the North Atlantic. You stand on a basalt ledge
15 metres above the sea. The cliff face behind you — undercut by ten
thousand years of wave action (@terrain_hydraulic_erosion) — drops sheer
to a tidal platform below. The ocean heaves: two-metre Atlantic swell,
cross-sea chop, wind ripple (@ocean_fft). Every wave face is a different
shade of grey-green in the pre-dawn, catching the first orange smear on
the eastern horizon.

Radiance cascades (@radiance_cascades) carry that orange smear into the
underside of the cliff overhang — a warm ambient glow where there would
otherwise be nothing. SSGI (@ssgi) picks up the bounce inside the crevice
at your feet, amber light finding the dark corners that probes miss.
A tidal pool at the foot of the ledge mirrors the sky through screen-space
reflections (@screen_space_reflection): the orange streak, the first star
not yet faded, a gannet banking 200 metres out.

Bioluminescent kelp (@glowing) rings the pool in pale blue, animated fronds
stirred by the surge. The @spatial_audio field puts the wave crash below,
the wind behind, the seabird ahead — you turn toward the sound before you
look.

This is the first time @ocean_fft, @terrain_hydraulic_erosion,
@radiance_cascades, @screen_space_reflection, and @ssgi appear together
in any A-009 stress-test or example file.

@version 0.1.0
@category stress-test, terrain, ocean, gi, post-processing, dawn
@traits @ocean_fft @terrain_hydraulic_erosion @radiance_cascades @screen_space_reflection @ssgi @glowing @animated @spatial_audio @collidable
@filed-by A-009 Example freshness + artist stress-test

Stress-Test: Eroded Shore at Dawn
A-009 — 2026-05-17

Five never-exercised traits under test (all ZERO prior examples):

@ocean_fft              — Tessendorf FFT ocean with 4-cascade wave simulation,
white-cap foam threshold, and sub-surface scattering tint.
The ocean's normal map updates at 60 Hz from GPU FFT.

@terrain_hydraulic_erosion — procedural coastline geometry carved by simulated
water flow. Tallus slopes, undercut sea arches, and
tidal pool hollows generated from an initial heightmap.

@radiance_cascades      — multi-scale 2D radiance cascade GI for the sky dome.
Four cascade levels: 1m / 4m / 16m / 64m resolution.
Dawn sky colour propagates as soft bounce into cliff faces.

@screen_space_reflection — SSR on wet stone ledges and tidal pools.
Ray-march depth buffer; temporal reprojection to
suppress flicker on glancing angles.

@ssgi                   — Screen-space global illumination for cliff crevices
and cave mouths. Captures amber sky bounce into shadowed
rock faces that GI probes miss at short range.

Well-exercised anchors (pull the zero-coverage traits into a proven context):
@glowing       — dawn horizon glow strip + bioluminescent kelp in tidal pools
@animated      — kelp fronds wave in surge; foam patches drift
@spatial_audio — wave crash + wind + distant seabird
@collidable    — player can stand on the shore ledge

Visual story:
04:58. First light over the North Atlantic. You stand on a basalt ledge
15 metres above the sea. The cliff face behind you — undercut by ten
thousand years of wave action (@terrain_hydraulic_erosion) — drops sheer
to a tidal platform below. The ocean heaves: two-metre Atlantic swell,
cross-sea chop, wind ripple (@ocean_fft). Every wave face is a different
shade of grey-green in the pre-dawn, catching the first orange smear on
the eastern horizon.

Radiance cascades (@radiance_cascades) carry that orange smear into the
underside of the cliff overhang — a warm ambient glow where there would
otherwise be nothing. SSGI (@ssgi) picks up the bounce inside the crevice
at your feet, amber light finding the dark corners that probes miss.
A tidal pool at the foot of the ledge mirrors the sky through screen-space
reflections (@screen_space_reflection): the orange streak, the first star
not yet faded, a gannet banking 200 metres out.

Bioluminescent kelp (@glowing) rings the pool in pale blue, animated fronds
stirred by the surge. The @spatial_audio field puts the wave crash below,
the wind behind, the seabird ahead — you turn toward the sound before you
look.

This is the first time @ocean_fft, @terrain_hydraulic_erosion,
@radiance_cascades, @screen_space_reflection, and @ssgi appear together
in any A-009 stress-test or example file.

HullFloor
description:
============================================================================
A-009 Stress Test — 2026-05-08
"Fracture Line"

NEVER-EXERCISED TRAITS UNDER TEST:
@emergent_spacetime — Provenance-weighted entanglement lattice. Exercises
initial_voxels=500, ricci_heatmap, force_layout_guard,
real_time_budget_ms constraint, and the seed path for
deterministic replay. The lattice forms the scene's
only interior light source — proving visual output, not
just silent physics.
@advanced_pbr       — Full PBR extension stack. Tests clearcoat (lacquered
composite hull plating), iridescence (thin-film oil-slick
on coolant tank surfaces), anisotropy (brushed titanium
floor grating), and transmission (blast-glass observation
window). Four sub-modes in one scene.
@advanced_texturing — Displacement + POM. Hull plate geometry uses tessellated
displacement (micrometeorite cratering); observation-dome
interior uses parallax-occlusion mapping with self-shadowed
surface scratches. Exercises both 'displacement' and 'pom'
TexMappingMode paths.

WELL-EXERCISED ANCHORS (binding the new traits into a living scene):
@emissive           — fracture corona and emergency strip lighting
@particle           — graviton static around the fracture point
@collidable         — all six hull walls for physics boundary
@animated           — slow axial tumble on the station module (no gyros left)
@anchor             — three emergency tether points, world-locked

SCENE STORY:
Station module ΔV-7 has been drifting in a 340 km orbit for six hours since
main propulsion died. The crew evacuated. What remains is a 12 × 12 × 4 m
pressurised box of matte-black composite and scratched titanium, still sealed.

In the geometric centre of the module, an entanglement experiment ran past
its containment budget. The ProvenanceNetwork is still live — 500 voxels
self-organising into an emergent distance metric, Ricci curvature visualised
as a heat gradient shifting from violet (low curvature) to amber (high).
The lattice pulses gently at the Hubble-correction frequency: ~0.03 Hz.

Hull plate interiors are lacquered carbon-fibre composite — clearcoat gloss
over a dark-grey base. Where coolant tanks ruptured, thin liquid films
dried into iridescent coatings on the aluminium panels: soap-bubble colours
cycling through the visible spectrum at different viewing angles. The floor
grating is brushed titanium, its anisotropy axis aligned with the extrusion
direction. The observation window is a 30 mm blast-glass panel — transmission
factor 0.88, chromatic dispersion just high enough to produce a faint rainbow
fringe at oblique incidence.

@advanced_texturing gives the hull plates their physical history: thousands
of micrometeorite craters 0.1–3 mm in diameter are encoded in a displacement
height-map tessellated to level 8. Inside the module, the observation-dome
ceiling uses POM (64 ray-march steps, self-shadowed) to render deep surface
scratches from the emergency egress sequence without adding geometry.

Three emergency tether clips are anchored to the hull — world-locked in the
pre-failure orientation — waiting for a salvage crew that may or may not
come.
============================================================================

name: HullPortSide
description:
============================================================================
A-009 Stress Test — 2026-05-08
"Fracture Line"

NEVER-EXERCISED TRAITS UNDER TEST:
@emergent_spacetime — Provenance-weighted entanglement lattice. Exercises
initial_voxels=500, ricci_heatmap, force_layout_guard,
real_time_budget_ms constraint, and the seed path for
deterministic replay. The lattice forms the scene's
only interior light source — proving visual output, not
just silent physics.
@advanced_pbr       — Full PBR extension stack. Tests clearcoat (lacquered
composite hull plating), iridescence (thin-film oil-slick
on coolant tank surfaces), anisotropy (brushed titanium
floor grating), and transmission (blast-glass observation
window). Four sub-modes in one scene.
@advanced_texturing — Displacement + POM. Hull plate geometry uses tessellated
displacement (micrometeorite cratering); observation-dome
interior uses parallax-occlusion mapping with self-shadowed
surface scratches. Exercises both 'displacement' and 'pom'
TexMappingMode paths.

WELL-EXERCISED ANCHORS (binding the new traits into a living scene):
@emissive           — fracture corona and emergency strip lighting
@particle           — graviton static around the fracture point
@collidable         — all six hull walls for physics boundary
@animated           — slow axial tumble on the station module (no gyros left)
@anchor             — three emergency tether points, world-locked

SCENE STORY:
Station module ΔV-7 has been drifting in a 340 km orbit for six hours since
main propulsion died. The crew evacuated. What remains is a 12 × 12 × 4 m
pressurised box of matte-black composite and scratched titanium, still sealed.

In the geometric centre of the module, an entanglement experiment ran past
its containment budget. The ProvenanceNetwork is still live — 500 voxels
self-organising into an emergent distance metric, Ricci curvature visualised
as a heat gradient shifting from violet (low curvature) to amber (high).
The lattice pulses gently at the Hubble-correction frequency: ~0.03 Hz.

Hull plate interiors are lacquered carbon-fibre composite — clearcoat gloss
over a dark-grey base. Where coolant tanks ruptured, thin liquid films
dried into iridescent coatings on the aluminium panels: soap-bubble colours
cycling through the visible spectrum at different viewing angles. The floor
grating is brushed titanium, its anisotropy axis aligned with the extrusion
direction. The observation window is a 30 mm blast-glass panel — transmission
factor 0.88, chromatic dispersion just high enough to produce a faint rainbow
fringe at oblique incidence.

@advanced_texturing gives the hull plates their physical history: thousands
of micrometeorite craters 0.1–3 mm in diameter are encoded in a displacement
height-map tessellated to level 8. Inside the module, the observation-dome
ceiling uses POM (64 ray-march steps, self-shadowed) to render deep surface
scratches from the emergency egress sequence without adding geometry.

Three emergency tether clips are anchored to the hull — world-locked in the
pre-failure orientation — waiting for a salvage crew that may or may not
come.

name: DesignPreviewMesh
description:
============================================================================
Stress-Test: Maker's Night Watch — Shared XR Fabrication Atelier
A-009 Phase 3 — 2026-05-20

Trait combo (fabrication-devices category: ZERO prior coverage in any example):

@sculpt_volume       (0 prior) — central design preview: the bracket being
manufactured floats above the workbench as a translucent
voxel mesh, 128-voxel resolution, rotating slowly so all
angles are inspectable without touching anything.

@printability_feedback (0 prior) — overlaid on the sculpt_volume preview.
Overhang > 45° lights orange. Unsupported islands glow
red. Bridge spans > 60 mm pulse yellow. Real-time update
when the design changes; dormant otherwise.

@fdm_target          (0 prior) — FDM printer head + in-progress print object.
Red PETG, 0.2 mm layers, gyroid infill. Gcode-driven
head movement animates in realtime. Current layer counter
drives the partial mesh visibility.

@resin_target        (0 prior) — MSLA resin VAT printer growing a translucent
architectural model. 405 nm UV, 50 µm layers. UV backlight
glows blue-violet through the FEP film; the platform
lifts by one layer every ~3.2 seconds.

@laser_cuttable      (0 prior) — acrylic panel inside the laser cutter.
55 % power, engraving circuit traces from an SVG.
The laser dot animates along the vector path; the engraved
traces emit a faint green glow (acrylic edge-light effect).

@fabrication_ready   (0 prior) — the finished PETG bracket resting on the
bench beside a caliper. Verified: true, dimensional
tolerance 0.3 mm. A subtle certification-blue pulse
distinguishes it from the in-progress prints.

Well-exercised anchors (pull zero-coverage traits into proven context):
@animated    (271 prior) — FDM head gcode path; resin platform lift;
laser dot SVG trace; sculpt mesh rotation
@glowing     (726 prior) — nozzle hot-end heat; resin UV bed;
laser dot; acrylic trace edge-light;
fabrication_ready certification pulse
@collidable  (664 prior) — workbench, floor, printer bodies, finished part
@spatial_audio (77 prior)— per-machine audio emitters: FDM stepper hum,
resin lift peel, laser servo traversal, shop ambience
@reactive    (62 prior)  — printability_feedback updates when design changes

Visual story:
03:22 AM. You are standing in a 60 m² basement maker-space. Three machines
are running. The air smells of hot PETG and UV resin.

To your left: an FDM printer is 26 % through a red bracket — layer 47 of 180.
The nozzle traces a gyroid infill pattern, the orange-red glow of the hot end
visible as it sweeps. You watch a layer complete. The print is deliberate,
accumulative. No drama, just process.

To your right: a resin MSLA printer. The VAT bottom glows blue-violet. Every
3 seconds, the build platform lifts one layer — a faint peeling sound as the
cured layer releases from the FEP film. A translucent architectural model is
half-formed, suspended upside-down from the platform: delicate arches and
columns in clear resin, each layer 50 µm, each one invisible from the last.

Behind you: a laser cutter traces circuit traces onto a green acrylic panel.
The dot moves fast — 180 mm/s — along conductor paths. The engraved channels
edge-light in neon green: acrylic carries the laser's wake.

Above the central workbench, a holographic mesh preview rotates: the bracket
in progress, 128-voxel resolution, semi-transparent. Orange zones mark the
two 50° overhangs the designer hasn't resolved yet. One island glows red —
it will detach mid-print if left unsupported. The designer is asleep. You
make a note.

03:22 AM. You are standing in a 60 m² basement maker-space. Three machines

cured layer releases from the FEP film. A translucent architectural model is
half-formed, suspended upside-down from the platform: delicate arches and
columns in clear resin, each layer 50 µm, each one invisible from the last.

Behind you: a laser cutter traces circuit traces onto a green acrylic panel.
The dot moves fast — 180 mm/s — along conductor paths. The engraved channels
edge-light in neon green: acrylic carries the laser's wake.

in progress, 128-voxel resolution, semi-transparent. Orange zones mark the
two 50° overhangs the designer hasn't resolved yet. One island glows red —
it will detach mid-print if left unsupported. The designer is asleep. You
make a note.

Black PETG, already sanded. It pulses once, slowly — a soft blue — confirming
it passed the dimensional check this afternoon: ±0.28 mm on all faces.

rhythmic chitter — and the resin printer's occasional peel.

name: PlazaFloor
description:
============================================================================
A-009 Stress Test — 2026-05-04
"Murmuration Market"

NEW TRAITS EXERCISED (zero prior coverage across all examples):
@crowd_sim        — GPU crowd: 4 000 agents flocking + goal-seeking
@navmesh_solver   — bakes the terraced amphitheater into a walkable mesh
@pose_estimation  — 4 drone cameras reading crowd body language overhead

Supporting traits (well-exercised, binding the new ones into a scene):
@glowing, @collidable, @physics, @spatial_audio, @billboard, @animated

SCENE STORY:
A living open-air bazaar carved into a sunken amphitheater.
4 000 visitors flow between merchant stalls like a murmuration of
starlings — drawn by @crowd_sim GPU flocking with goal weights tuned
to stall positions. The @navmesh_solver bakes the terraced geometry
(stairs, bridges, narrow alleys) so the crowd moves realistically,
not through walls.

Four @pose_estimation drones orbit overhead, each reading body
language from a different quadrant. Their aggregate excitement scores
— derived from arm-raised ratio and inter-person distance — feed back
as dynamic goal weights, shifting crowd flow toward the most animated
cluster. The crowd becomes self-organizing: energy in one corner
propagates outward as a wave of attention.

ARTISTIC INTENT:
At steady state the plaza breathes. Vendors near excited clusters
attract more visitors, who raise their arms, which the drones detect,
which attracts more visitors. A feedback loop between human pose and
crowd dynamics — legible, beautiful, emergent.

COMPILE TARGETS:
holoscript compile <file> --target webgpu   (preferred — GPU crowd)
holoscript compile <file> --target unity    (HDRP crowd instancing)
holoscript compile <file> --target unreal   (Mass Entity + MetaHuman)
============================================================================

starlings — drawn by @crowd_sim GPU flocking with goal weights tuned
to stall positions. The @navmesh_solver bakes the terraced geometry
(stairs, bridges, narrow alleys) so the crowd moves realistically,
not through walls.

language from a different quadrant. Their aggregate excitement scores
— derived from arm-raised ratio and inter-person distance — feed back
as dynamic goal weights, shifting crowd flow toward the most animated
cluster. The crowd becomes self-organizing: energy in one corner
propagates outward as a wave of attention.

At steady state the plaza breathes. Vendors near excited clusters
attract more visitors, who raise their arms, which the drones detect,
which attracts more visitors. A feedback loop between human pose and
crowd dynamics — legible, beautiful, emergent.

name: render_controller
description:
============================================================
Stress-Test: Neural Memory Theater
A009 — 2026-05-01

Never-exercised traits under test:
@multiview_gaussian_renderer — foveated multi-user Gaussian
splat rendering with per-view
quality adaptation
@neural_animation            — ML locomotion and body motion
applied to volumetric figures
@volumetric                  — pointcloud / Gaussian-splat
3D scan playback at runtime

Well-exercised anchors:
@glowing  @collidable  @animated  @physics

Visual story:
You step into a black-box theater. The stage is empty save
for four floating memory-frames: 3D scans of past performances,
each a volumetric ghost rendered in Gaussian splat mode. The
renderer adapts quality per viewer — full fidelity at your
fovea, gracefully coarsening at the periphery. Each ghost is
neural-animated: the motion model infers the performer's next
gesture from their body state, so no two viewings are alike.
A slow haze of volumetric cloud fills the stage floor. The
ghosts breathe, shift weight, occasionally turn toward you as
if they remember being seen.

This is the first time @multiview_gaussian_renderer,
@neural_animation, and @volumetric are exercised together.
The test verifies: (a) foveated blend config parses as a
nested object, (b) neural animation config validates the
AnimationModel enum path, (c) volumetric src + renderMode
parse inside a composition.
============================================================

A009 — 2026-04-29

Well-exercised anchors:
@glowing  @collidable  @physics  @animated

Visual story:
You are inside an observatory carved into the rock of a near-Earth
asteroid. The control console hums under warm photometric lamp glow.
At T=0 the dome iris begins to open — a cinematic sequence cuts
between the dome gears, the widening star field, and your hands at
the controls. As the telescope arm tilts toward the ecliptic plane
(elevation 23.4°) the sonification trait begins to moan a low
drone: a perfect fifth built from the two brightest stars in
the current field of view, their angular separation mapped linearly
from 80 Hz to 440 Hz. The observatory has never been more alive.
============================================================

description:
============================================================
Stress-Test: Sunken Archive
A009 — 2026-05-02

Never-exercised traits under test:
@holomap_reconstruct          — active 3D reconstruction session on the
carved stone tablets, consuming camera
frames as the drone orbits
@holomap_camera_trajectory    — drone's orbital flight path fed into the
reconstruction pipeline
@holomap_anchor_context       — seabed survey markers that anchor the
session's spatial reference frame
@holomap_drift_correction     — compensates for current-induced drift in
the drone's pose estimates
@holomap_splat_output         — the output panel: emerging Gaussian splat
model rendered in real time as scan data
arrives
@speech                       — researcher AI narrates discoveries as new
structure is reconstructed

Well-exercised anchors (not under test):
@glowing  @collidable  @networked  @grabbable  @physics

Visual story:
Twelve metres below the Aegean surface, a submersible drone traces slow
ellipses around a sunken archive — a trove of carved marble tablets that
went under in 365 CE. The drone's camera feeds raw frames into a
@holomap_reconstruct session anchored to four survey markers bolted to the
seabed. A @holomap_drift_correction module watches the trajectory, nudging
pose estimates whenever the current pushes the drone off its programmed
orbit. As each orbit completes another ring of geometry materialises on the
output panel — a real-time @holomap_splat_output hanging in the water
column above, glowing amber against the blue void. A disembodied @speech
voice — the researcher AI observing remotely — calls out whenever a new
tablet face emerges: "Alpha-seven visible. Greek text, second century."
Collaborators on the surface can grab the splat panel, rotate it, pin
annotations. The scene is a networked multi-user excavation in slow motion.

This is the first time any of the five holomap_* traits and @speech are
exercised together. The test verifies:
(a) holomap_reconstruct's session_id / input_mode parse as typed fields
(b) holomap_camera_trajectory's path_mode + orbit_radius parse as nested config
(c) holomap_anchor_context's anchor array syntax with position tuples
(d) holomap_drift_correction's correction_strategy enum parses
(e) holomap_splat_output's output_mode + lod_levels parse
(f) speech event map with variable substitution parses inside a composition
============================================================

name: stage_floor
description:
============================================================
Stress-Test: Three Voices — AI Performer Troupe
A009 — 2026-05-01

Never-exercised traits under test:
@choreography      — multi-step movement orchestration with
HITL gates and fallback plans
@lip_sync          — phoneme-driven viseme animation
@emotional_voice   — emotion-modulated TTS voice synthesis
@avatar_embodiment — IK-tracked avatar body with emotion
directive integration
@spatial_persona   — persistent spatial identity, proximity
visibility, gesture mirroring

Well-exercised anchors:
@glowing  @animated  @accessible  @collidable

Visual story:
A minimalist stage: white cyclorama, three pools of colored
light. Three AI performers stand in the light pools, each
assigned a single emotional register that cannot leave them.

ANGER speaks in clipped declarative sentences — short, loud,
percussive. Her lips follow every word. She advances on the
audience then retreats, pacing, never still.

GRIEF moves slowly, barely at all. She rarely speaks; when
she does the voice wavers at the consonants. Her spatial
persona flickers at the boundary of visibility — you have
to stand close to see her properly.

WONDER never stops talking. She gestures upward, turns her
head toward sounds nobody else hears, addresses objects as
if they are friends. Her persona is always fully visible,
arms wide.

A choreography controller sequences their positions across
nine named stages, pausing at an HITL gate on stage 5 —
a deliberate human-approval pause built into the script.

This exercises: nested choreography step config, multi-trait
composition on avatar objects, lip_sync method enum, and the
spatial_persona proximity_radius field.
============================================================

name: MoonRise
description:
============================================================================
A-009 Stress Test — 2026-05-07
"Resonant Tide Pool at Dusk"

NEVER-EXERCISED TRAITS UNDER TEST:
@bioluminescent  — pulsing emissive surface driven by time + proximity +
spatial pattern. Exercises all three pattern modes:
'perlin' (water surface, algae), 'voronoi' (jellyfish
bells), 'solid' (anemone crown). Also exercises
the proximity-observer event path and bpm range 6–24.
@buoyancy        — Archimedes' principle physics. Exercises two density
regimes: near-neutral buoyancy (jellyfish ρ ≈ 1020
in seawater ρ = 1025) and strongly positive (algae
ρ = 200, driftwood-class). Exercises flow_direction,
splash_effect, and the on_splash / on_submerge event
chain that triggers particle bursts.

WELL-EXERCISED ANCHORS (binding the new traits into a living scene):
@animated        — jellyfish bell contraction cycle (0.6 s period)
@particle        — surface shimmer, splash bursts, bioluminescent sparkle
@spatial_audio   — low ocean drone + tide-pool resonance cavity
@collidable      — basalt rocks defining the pool walls
@emissive        — distant moonrise disc providing the only top light

SCENE STORY:
It is 20:14 on a Pacific coast evening. The tide has retreated,
leaving a metre-deep pool in a shelf of black basalt. The last
amber light fades from the western sky — and the pool wakes up.

Moon jellyfish (Aurelia aurita) drift near the surface, their
translucent bells pulsing at 10 beats per minute. Buoyancy keeps
them suspended just below the meniscus; a gentle long-shore
current nudges them south at 0.04 m/s. When a jellyfish bell
breaks the surface, a tiny splash triggers a bioluminescent burst
from the disturbed plankton — sparks of cold cyan fire that fade
over 800 ms.

Sea anemones (Anthopleura elegantissima) ring the shallows,
anchored to the rock walls, their crowns in solid-mode bioluminescence
— a steady magenta glow that needs no temporal modulation because
the animal is already at rest, respiring in the dark.

Drifting algae mats (Ulva lactuca, sea lettuce) bob at the
surface: density 200 kg/m³ in seawater means they sit mostly
above the waterline. Their perlin-patterned bioluminescence shifts
cyan-green as they rotate in the current — the spatial coordinates
change so the pattern drifts, giving the impression of living light
flowing through the blades.

Above, a rising moon is the only light source not biological —
an emissive disc at 200 m altitude providing 0.15 lux of cold
blue-white fill. It is enough to see the rocks by, but the real
illumination comes from below.

ARTISTIC INTENT:
Bioluminescence is darkness made visible. The scene asks: what if
the organisms themselves are the lamps? Every light source here
belongs to a living thing (or a celestial body standing in for one).
@buoyancy grounds the scene in physics: the jellyfish don't float
because they're objects, they float because seawater is denser than
their mesoglea. The difference is felt in the slow drift, the
reluctant splash when they reach the surface, the way the current
accumulates them against the south wall of the pool.

COMPILE TARGET: webgpu
Transparent mesh alpha-sort required for jellyfish bell stacking.
Particle count: ~2 400 (surface shimmer 2 000 + splash burst 400).
============================================================================

translucent bells pulsing at 10 beats per minute. Buoyancy keeps
them suspended just below the meniscus; a gentle long-shore
current nudges them south at 0.04 m/s. When a jellyfish bell
breaks the surface, a tiny splash triggers a bioluminescent burst
from the disturbed plankton — sparks of cold cyan fire that fade
over 800 ms.

Sea anemones (Anthopleura elegantissima) ring the shallows,
anchored to the rock walls, their crowns in solid-mode bioluminescence
— a steady magenta glow that needs no temporal modulation because
the animal is already at rest, respiring in the dark.

surface: density 200 kg/m³ in seawater means they sit mostly
above the waterline. Their perlin-patterned bioluminescence shifts

change so the pattern drifts, giving the impression of living light
flowing through the blades.
